messages.author: e83d54ec65b5b8e6
messages.subject: different behavior in dplyr and plyr
parts:
As I posted already I need to use summarising function using function with matrix arguments.
I tried to convert what I have from plyr do dplyr, and it did not work.

Here is a simplified example
We use this dataframe

 
   set.seed(100)
   varnames <- paste("var",1:10,sep="")
   varshort <- varnames[3:5]
   vara <- rep(c("a","b"),10)
   mat <- matrix(rnorm(200),20,10)
   mydf <- data.frame(vara,mat)
   names(mydf)[2:11]<-varnames




Using plyr, the following three examples work

testdf1a <- ddply(mydf,.(vara),summarise,sss=sum(cbind(var3,var4,var5)))

testdf2a <- ddply(mydf,.(vara),summarise,sss=
                    sum(as.matrix(as.data.frame(mget(varshort)))))

testdf3a <- ddply(mydf,.(vara),summarise,sss=
                    sum(eval(parse(text=
                                     paste("cbind(",paste(varshort,collapse=","),")")))))


But when I simply translate these examples into dplyr syntax, the second and the third one do not work any more:


testdf1b <-  mydf %.% group_by(vara) %.%
  summarise(sss=sum(cbind(var3,var4,var5)))

testdf2b <-  mydf %.% group_by(vara) %.%
  summarise(sss=sum(as.matrix(as.data.frame(mget(varshort)))))

testdf3b <-  mydf %.% group_by(vara) %.%
  summarise(sss=sum(eval(parse(text=
                      paste("cbind(",paste(varshort,collapse=","),")")))))

The error message for the second assignment is

Error: value for ‘var3’ not found

It seems that in plyr, the enviroment used within the ddply function call contains the objects needed,
but in dplyr, the names given as strings and evaluated either by mget or by eval(parse(text=.....
cannot be resolved,

Is there a way of accomplishing what I need, namely extracting as large set of variables and combining these into a matrix to 
pass them to a function?

messages.author: 004520bffd484721
messages.subject: Re: different behavior in dplyr and plyr
parts:
Use `do` to subset to the variables you want, calculate the sum, and return the result as a data frame. According to the help for `do`, the result must always be a data frame. 

mydf %>%
  group_by(vara) %>%
  do(subset(., select = varshort) %>% sum %>% data.frame(sss = .))


If you don't need to set the variable name (`sss`), then you can replace `data.frame(sss = .)` with `data.frame`.

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: different behavior in dplyr and plyr
parts:
Hi Erich,

I'm not sure what problem you are trying to solve. It's true that
things work differently in dply than in plyr, but you've been given
the tools you need to carry out the operation you described, namely
'do'. For example,

dfgr %>%
do(data.frame(sss = (function(x,y)sum(x*y))
(as.matrix(.[c("X1","X2")]),
as.matrix(.[c("X3","X4")]))))

produces the same result as

summarise(dfgr,sss=(function(x,y)sum(x*y))(cbind(X1,X2),cbind(X3,X4)))

Best,
Ista
